plan: With 3 bidders and this mechanism functioning as a second-price auction (since the clock auction with sealed exit bids results in the winner paying the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, which maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities.

Since this functions as a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I'd pay the competitor's bid, not my own. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, truthful bidding is optimal.

Since this auction functions like a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid/exit price), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $32 ensures I win whenever the prize is worth more to me than to competitors, and I pay only the second-highest bid, which will always be at or below my value—guaranteeing non-negative profit if I win. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions.
